answer: No third-party human has used the app. Production holds 63 posts and one of them is a person's: a photo from the owner's own account on 31 August, 2 views, radius decaying. Firebase Analytics is linked at the project level and has never received an event because no client ships the SDK, and no feedback channel has ever received a message. The simulation did run in the last 24 h: 3,412 synthetic browser events from five runner actors, 13 posts made through the real composer, then every live cohort actor stopped. 63 pops moved in the window, all through tonight's radiusHistory backfill (242 entries) and one hourly decay step; none of the movement came from a person.

signals.title: The first message to anyone never sent
signals.body: The synthetic testers' direct-message step failed 110 times and never once succeeded. The cause was in the app, not the runner: the client read the message document before writing the batch, the participant lookup returned nothing for a thread that did not exist yet, and the rules denied it. This is the strongest product defect the Test Center has surfaced, and it surfaced as a step failure, not as feedback. Production now has its first thread.
signals.evidence: synthetic-runner.log "step send-dm failed" ×110, " messaged " ×0; iOS commit 8f28662b

signals.title: Testers never reach the hold menu
signals.body: The hold gesture failed 131 times in the synthetic journeys, 123 of them "did not settle on hold-menu (saw feed)"; it is the current error of one runner actor. Whether this is a runner selector problem or a real discoverability problem for a person holding the cube is not established by any evidence found. Worth a human test.

signals.title: A newcomer with nothing nearby sees an empty app
signals.body: Apple rejected the app as "not complete" because radius-gated delivery meant a reviewer outside every post's radius saw nothing. The 29 official posts reach the whole planet to fix that. The reviewer's own words are not stored in any repository; only a developer's paraphrase survives. The same emptiness awaits any first user in a quiet area.

signals.title: Silent front-end failures would be invisible to the desk
signals.body: The runner captures console errors and page errors in memory only (a 20-line tail) and the session documents carry no such fields. Across the whole log it recorded zero of either, which is either good news or a blind spot; today it cannot tell which.
signals.evidence: testSyntheticBrowserSessions schema; runner log pageerror ×0, console.error ×0

signals.title: Infrastructure, not product
signals.body: Twenty connection refusals to the RN shell on 8081, one 75-second page timeout, and 32,230 sandbox "blocked" verdicts are the runner's environment and its safety net doing their jobs. The scheduler cannot restart a runner that is down by design, so once the cohort stops it stays stopped until someone starts it.

gaps: No analytics data at all, on any platform; the GA4 property was not opened from this session, and code-wise nothing has ever sent it an event.
No human feedback text anywhere readable from this Mac.
Human activity is one post by the owner's account; no third-party human account exists.
The App Review rejection survives only as a paraphrase; the guideline number and Resolution Center thread are not stored.
The origin of the like and view counts on official and cohort posts was not traced past "seeded or simulation-driven"; they must not be read as human engagement.
The Test Center page was down, so its rendered dashboard was not inspected; the report is built from its source and the same collections it reads.
Whether the 131 hold-menu failures reflect a human discoverability problem or a runner selector problem is undetermined.

proposals.title: A "Send feedback" row in web Settings
proposals.why: No human can tell the desk anything: no app has a feedback row, form or mail link, and the in-app browser blocks mailto:. The backend that would store it already exists and has never been called.
proposals.evidence: feedback: In-app "Send feedback" received 0; testFeedback received 0; grep submitBetaFeedback → definition only (PoplurApp/src/services/testControl.ts:619)
proposals.change: Add a Settings row in poplur-clay-map with the three fields the testFeedback backend already stores (finding, liked, improve), calling the existing beta-feedback action. The desk's "What testers are saying" section already renders those documents.
proposals.risk: Low: a new write path to an existing callable whose rule already exists. Needs a rules-deploy check and a 64-character cap on free text.

proposals.title: Prompt the "Share closed-beta activity" switch once after first login
proposals.why: 0 of 5 accounts have consented, so the human telemetry collection is empty and "Who is testing right now" has never had a row. The switch is opt-in and nobody has found it.
proposals.evidence: users where testActivityConsent EQUAL true → 0; testActivity count → 0
proposals.change: Show the switch once on the first post-login launch of a beta build, defaulting to off, and record the answer on users/{uid} so the prompt never repeats.
proposals.risk: Medium: a consent prompt is a product surface whose wording needs review; a wrong default would collect without consent.
